questions.prompt: What happens when you comment '@claude fix the failing date test' on a GitHub issue (with the integration installed)?

options.text: Claude replies with advice but cannot touch code
A Claude session runs inside GitHub Actions: it clones the repo, works on a branch, and pushes commits or opens a PR for review
Claude edits the default branch directly with no review step
It opens Claude Code on your laptop

questions.explanation: The mention triggers a real working session in CI. Crucially the output is a branch/PR — reviewable, revertable — not silent direct pushes to main (c).

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson call headless claude -p 'the building block' of all these integrations?

options.text: Because every integration — Actions, schedulers, this very app's terminal — is ultimately a script invoking Claude non-interactively with a prompt, scoped tools, and captured output
Because headless mode is the only free tier
Because -p disables permissions, which automation requires

questions.explanation: One primitive, many costumes: prompt in, permitted tools, output back. Permissions still apply fully (d is exactly wrong — automation makes scoped permissions MORE important, not less).

questions.prompt: Which statement about OpenClaw is accurate?

options.text: It is Anthropic's official mobile client for Claude Code

It is a third-party multi-channel agent gateway — a persistent agent reachable through chat channels, configured with persona files like SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, and HEARTBEAT.md — and not an Anthropic product
It is a Claude model variant fine-tuned for messaging apps
It is the protocol underlying MCP

questions.explanation: OpenClaw sits in the third-party ecosystem built ON the building block: a standing agent with file-based persona and schedule config. Because it isn't Anthropic's, its security and trust model is yours to vet before granting credentials.
